subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron quarantine recovery archives be silently capped at five files, or should retention and cleanup be owned by a recoverable Doctor/operator workflow?
rationale: The code can implement either approach, but choosing whether recovery evidence may be deleted and how operators retrieve it is a durable product and persistence-policy decision.

options.title: Use Doctor-owned retention and recovery
options.body: Keep bounded reads and overflow rotation, but make archive inspection and cleanup a visible Doctor/operator contract before deleting recovery files.

options.title: Approve fixed five-file pruning
options.body: Accept the current silent oldest-first deletion policy as the supported retention contract and document the recovery-data tradeoff.

options.title: Defer archive rotation
options.body: Land only the bounded read/write behavior and leave capped-sidecar recovery unavailable until a retention policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Use Doctor-owned retention and recovery
recommendation.body: Keep bounded reads and overflow rotation, but make archive inspection and cleanup a visible Doctor/operator contract before deleting recovery files.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly requests this archive-retention decision from this person, although the repository history trail could not be independently confirmed.
